group.title: Health and the body
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: The parts of your body that make you move.
wrong: A muscle is a kind of bone in your ear that you hear with.

words.meaning: One of the hard parts inside your body.
examples: He broke a {bone} in his arm.
wrong: A bone is a soft part of your skin.

words.meaning: The organ inside your head that you think with.
wrong: You think with your stomach, not your brain.

words.meaning: The red liquid that moves around your body.
wrong: Blood is a blue drink.

words.meaning: One of the two organs in your chest that you breathe with.
wrong: You breathe with your lungs in your feet.

words.meaning: The inside of your neck, where food goes down.
wrong: Your throat is at the end of your arm.

words.meaning: A cut or injury on the body.
wrong: A wound is a medicine that makes you feel better.

words.meaning: A dark mark on your skin after you hit something.
examples: I have a big {bruise} on my leg.
wrong: A bruise is a white flower.

words.meaning: Red spots on the skin.
wrong: A rash is a kind of drink.

words.meaning: A small round piece of medicine that you swallow.
wrong: A pill is a cream you put on your skin.

words.meaning: Medical care for an illness or injury.
wrong: Treatment is the illness, not the care.

words.meaning: When a doctor cuts open the body to repair something.
examples: He had an {operation} on his knee.
wrong: An operation is a pill you take with water.

words.meaning: A pain that continues for some time.
examples: I have an {ache} in my back.
wrong: An ache is a pleasant feeling of joy.

words.meaning: Painful, often because of an injury or illness.
examples: My feet are {sore} after the walk.
wrong: My leg is sore, so it doesn’t hurt at all.

words.meaning: A medicine or treatment that makes an illness go away.
examples: There’s no {cure} for the common cold.
wrong: A cure is something that makes an illness worse.

words.meaning: To become healthy again after an injury.
wrong: The wound healed, so it got worse.

words.meaning: To take air into your body and let it out.
wrong: Fish breathe air on land.

words.meaning: To push air out of your nose suddenly, with a loud noise.
wrong: I sneeze through my ears.

words.meaning: To make food or drink go down your throat.
wrong: I swallowed the pill by keeping it in my hand.

words.meaning: To fall down because you suddenly become unconscious.
wrong: He fainted, so he stayed awake and stood up.

words.meaning: The food you usually eat.
examples: A healthy {diet} has lots of fruit.
wrong: A diet is a kind of exercise you do with a ball.

words.meaning: A natural substance in food that you need to be healthy.
wrong: A vitamin is a type of illness.

words.meaning: A unit that measures how much energy is in food.
wrong: A calorie is a unit for measuring distance.

words.meaning: Healthy and strong because of exercise.
examples: She runs every day to stay {fit}.
wrong: He is very fit, so he can’t walk up the stairs.

words.meaning: How heavy someone or something is.
wrong: My weight is how tall I am.

words.meaning: Heavier than is healthy.
examples: The doctor said I was a little {overweight}.
wrong: She is overweight, so she is too thin.

words.meaning: A feeling of worry caused by problems or too much work.
wrong: Stress is a feeling of total calm.

words.meaning: An illness that lasts a long time.
wrong: A condition is a kind of hospital bed.

words.meaning: An illness of people, animals or plants.
wrong: A disease is a sign of perfect health.

words.meaning: The state of being ill.
wrong: Illness is when you feel strong and healthy.

words.meaning: A very small living thing that causes illness.
examples: The flu is caused by a {virus}.
wrong: A virus is a vitamin that keeps you well.

words.meaning: Having a baby growing inside the body.
examples: She is {pregnant} with her second child.
wrong: He is pregnant with his grandfather.

words.meaning: A place where people go to see a doctor.
examples: I went to the {clinic} for a checkup.
wrong: A clinic is a shop that sells shoes.

words.meaning: Simple help given to an injured person before a doctor comes.
wrong: First aid is the last thing a doctor does after surgery.

words.meaning: A small sticky strip you put on a cut.
wrong: A plaster is a medicine you drink.

words.meaning: A mark left on the skin after a wound heals.
examples: He has a {scar} on his chin.
wrong: A scar is a fresh wound that is still bleeding.

words.meaning: The regular beat of your heart that you feel in your wrist.
wrong: A pulse is the color of your skin.

words.meaning: Not awake and not able to see or feel.
examples: He was {unconscious} for a few minutes after the fall.
wrong: She was unconscious, so she talked to everyone.

words.meaning: To stop something from happening.
wrong: We prevented the fire by starting it.

words.meaning: Keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy.
wrong: Hygiene means never washing.
